title: Geometry and topology of algebraic gerbes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Algebraic stacks and algebraic spaces over $S$ use [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-trf-algebraic-space], with 2-fibre products as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] and point spaces as in [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open]. Let $p:\mathcal X\to Q$ be a gerbe with $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack and $Q$ an algebraic space. A map $p:\mathcal X\to Q$ to an algebraic space is a gerbe if for every scheme $T\to Q$ its fibre groupoid has objects fppf locally on $T$, and any two objects of that fibre groupoid are isomorphic fppf locally on $T$ [def-pc-fppf-site]. Then $p$ is surjective and smooth. More explicitly, for every smooth surjective scheme atlas $u:U\to\mathcal X$, the composite $pu:U\to Q$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For every algebraic stack $\mathcal T/S$ and morphism $\mathcal T\to Q$, the projection induces a homeomorphism $|\mathcal X\times_Q\mathcal T|\to|\mathcal T|$. No reducedness, Noetherian, quasi-compactness or inertia-finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The gerbe condition is preserved by base change to a scheme $V\to Q$: its lift groupoids over $T\to V$ are precisely those over the composite $T\to Q$. The same observation applies to $\mathcal P=\mathcal X\times_Q\mathcal T\to\mathcal T$, whose objects are pairs with an isomorphism over $Q$. The fibre products are algebraic stacks by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. For any field object $t:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal T$, local nonemptiness gives an fppf covering of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ with lifts. Choose a point on a nonempty member and its residue field $L$; this gives a lift over $L/K$. Thus $|\mathcal P|\to|\mathcal T|$ is surjective, including $p$ itself.

source.place: Tags 06QE (lemma-base-change-gerbe), 06R9 (lemma-gerbe-bijection-points), surjectivity and explicit base-change argument

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary smooth surjective scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal X$ and an etale scheme chart $V\to Q$. Put $\mathcal G=\mathcal X\times_QV$ and $U_V=U\times_QV$; the latter is a scheme by the representable diagonal of $Q$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The atlas base changes to a smooth surjective map $U_V\to\mathcal G$ by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The gerbe condition gives an fppf cover $\{V_i\to V\}$ and objects $x_i\in\mathcal G(V_i)$. Set $\mathcal G_i=\mathcal G\times_VV_i$, $U_i=U_V\times_VV_i$ and $W_i=U_i\times_{\mathcal G_i}V_i$. By [lem-sfb-neutral-gerbe-section-fppf], the section $V_i\to\mathcal G_i$ is representable, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Consequently $W_i$ is an algebraic space, $W_i\to U_i$ has those three properties, and $W_i\to V_i$ is smooth as the base change of the atlas. These base changes use [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus].

source.place: Tag 06QG (lemma-gerbe-with-section)(3); Tag 0DLS (lemma-smooth-quotient-stack), diagram behind the source-descent argument

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $Z_i\to W_i$. The calculus [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] makes $Z_i\to U_i$ surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, and $Z_i\to V_i$ smooth. Both $U_i$ and $V_i$ are schemes, so [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] gives $U_i\to V_i$ smooth. By [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality] on the scheme target $V$, smoothness descends from all $U_i\to V_i$ to $U_V\to V$. This holds for every etale scheme chart $V\to Q$, hence $U\to Q$ is smooth by the chart test. Since the original atlas was arbitrary, $p$ is smooth in the atlas sense, and every composite $U\to Q$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by the same calculus. It is surjective: step 1 lifts each field-valued point to $\mathcal X$ after extension, and the atlas lifts that object after a further extension. This proves every geometric clause without asserting smoothness of a gerbe section.

Fix $\mathcal T\to Q$ and write $b:\mathcal P\to\mathcal T$ for the projection. To check injectivity on points, suppose field-valued objects $(x_1,t_1,\alpha_1)$ and $(x_2,t_2,\alpha_2)$ have the same image class in $|\mathcal T|$. By [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open], pass to a common field $M$ and choose an isomorphism $t_1\simeq t_2$. Using it and the two $\alpha_i$, view $x_1,x_2$ as objects of the same gerbe fibre over the map $\operatorname{Spec}M\to Q$. Local connectedness gives an fppf covering on which they are isomorphic in that fibre. Taking a point of a nonempty member yields a field extension $N/M$ and an isomorphism compatible with the chosen isomorphism of the $t_i$. By the explicit triple description [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], these are isomorphic objects of $\mathcal P(N)$. Thus they give the same point. Combined with step 1 this proves bijectivity of $|b|$.

source.place: Tag 06R9 (lemma-gerbe-bijection-points), injectivity: details of the omitted field-extension argument

proof.text: Continuity of $|b|$ follows from [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open]. Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $A\to\mathcal T$, set $\mathcal B=\mathcal P\times_{\mathcal T}A=\mathcal X\times_QA$, and choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $Z\to\mathcal B$. These products are algebraic by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. Steps 2--3 apply to the gerbe $\mathcal B\to A$, and show $Z\to A$ flat and locally of finite presentation. Its point map is open by [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open]. For open $O\subseteq|\mathcal P|$, let $O_Z$ be its inverse image in $|Z|$, open by continuity. Then $|A\to\mathcal T|^{-1}(|b|(O))$, equals the image of $O_Z$ in $|A|$. For the nontrivial inclusion, a point of $A$ and a point in $O$ with the same image in $\mathcal T$ have representatives with isomorphic images after common field extension. Their pair with that isomorphism gives a point of $\mathcal B$; the atlas $Z$ lifts it after further extension. The lift is in $O_Z$. The other inclusion follows from commutativity. Thus this inverse image is open, and the atlas criterion for $A\to\mathcal T$ makes $|b|(O)$ open. A continuous open bijection is a homeomorphism: its inverse takes the open set $O$ to the open set $|b|(O)$.
